column3: The Hebrew pictures abiding as spending the night.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add You are before my refuge as BSB does.
The Hebrew first names a wing or pinion in the singular and pictures truth as shield and armor; BSB says feathers and rampart.
The Hebrew leaves the subject of not drawing near unnamed; BSB supplies no harm.
The Hebrew says You, LORD, my refuge, then you made the Most High your dwelling; BSB rearranges these clauses.
The Hebrew has palms and carrying; BSB says lift you up in their hands.
The Hebrew names a dragon or great serpent in the final term; BSB says serpent.
The Hebrew pictures protection as setting him on high.
The Hebrew says I am with him in trouble rather than will be as BSB does.
